description: Wire fixtures for the sync contract, shared by every lane: the server drives them through HTTP, the device through its fake client, so a drift in the contract is caught here and not when the parts are first put together. Change them only together with libs/protocol/sync.ts.

fixtures.name: cursor-ack
fixtures.description: Acknowledges the highest serverSeq applied across all scopes, and is answered with 204 and no body. The other half of T-C-6 is a negative: there is no backfill endpoint and no backfill response shape — a new scope starts at 0 and is pulled (see pull-new-scope.json).

fixtures.name: hlc-format
fixtures.description: The HLC as it travels: physical unix milliseconds zero-padded to 15 digits, counter to 5, then the device id, which may itself contain colons. The padding is the point — the server compares the column as text, and that order has to be the domain order. Times beside them are UTC ISO 8601 with milliseconds (Д-17).

fixtures.name: optional-fields
fixtures.description: Every optional and nullable field at its edge, so both sides read them the same way: a pull request without limit, a delete tombstone whose data is null, a row whose nullable fields are all null, an empty text, an empty page with no scopes advanced, and an accepted result with no detail.

fixtures.name: pull-new-scope
fixtures.description: A course the student has just been enrolled on. The client has no position for it, the server reports it in scopes, and its history arrives through this ordinary pull. There is no backfill endpoint: this fixture IS the backfill.

fixtures.name: pull-page
fixtures.description: A pull page mixing two scopes: the course content going down and the student own rows. hasMore is true, so cursors carry the position each scope reached.

fixtures.name: push-mixed
fixtures.description: A batch whose rows are answered one by one: results has the length of changes and the same order, and a refusal leaves its neighbours applied.

fixtures.name: push-rejections
fixtures.description: Every rejection reason, once each. The work stays on the device in all seven cases: a refusal is a state of the row, never a lost edit.

fixtures.name: push-restamped
fixtures.description: serverHlc comes back on every accepted row, not only when it differs. Here the first row is a genuine repeat (same stamp, same body) and keeps its HLC; the second arrived from a device whose clock is a year fast, or whose id is shared with another phone restored from the same backup, and the server restamped it. Both records are kept; neither write is swallowed as an imagined repeat.

fixtures.name: request-errors
fixtures.description: The failures that are not per-row. Too many scopes is refused with a code rather than answered with a silently truncated list (Д-20).
